surface_mechanism_description: The surface reduction treatments, including hydrogen plasma treatment and rapid thermal anneal in hydrogen ambient, reduce the nitrogen content in the surface layer of the TaN x ultrathin film. This process forms a new chemical phase with a very small nitrogen content, possibly TaNx, which enhances the adhesion between the TaN x film and the Cu overlayer. The increase in the Ta/N atomic ratio in the RTA-treated TaN x thin film significantly improves the adhesion with the Cu layer.
evidence: The text discusses the formation of a new chemical phase with a very small nitrogen content, possibly TaNx, after RTA treatment. It also mentions the presence of oxygen-containing states due to oxidation of the PE-ALD TaN x thin film and the increase in the Ta/N atomic ratio after reduction treatments.
